0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 2 ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institu tion on 5 February 1985, after the draft finalized by the Solid Electrical Insulating Materials had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. .^, ~. ..,. 0.2 This standard deals with determination of thermal endurance' &f insulating varnishes by three different methods, covered in a series .\ comprising the following three parts: Part I Electric strength method, Part 2 Measurement of loss of mass, and Part `3 Bond strength by helical coil method. 0.3 This standard ( Part 2 ) covers the method of determining relative thermal endurance of insulating varnishes by measurement of loss Of mass. 0.4 In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from DIN 46456 - Varnishes and resins for electrical insulation - Impregnating varnishes - requiremects, test methods, issued by Deutsches Institut fiir Normung.

2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard,

the definitions given in IS : 10026

( Part 1 ) - 198 l* shall apply. 3. TEST SPECIMEN
3.1 Glass Cloth Panels - The glass cloth panels shall be cut from continuous filament, woven glass free from alkali 0'1 mm to 0'18 mm thick with a weight per unit area of 90 g/m" to 140 g/m2 and with 20 to 26 ends and 16 to 24 picks per centimetre.

The glass cloth shall be heat cleaned to remove binders. cloth should not contain residual size more than 0'2 percent.
NOTE - A suggested heat cleaning procedure consists of heating hours at 25CPC and 24 hours at 400�C. CALrE.r_ - Heating above 45a"C may damage the cloth.

the cloth 24

;, ; li+h~ panel of glass dbth shal1 be 15 X 30 cm with the 30 cm dimeusron parallel to the warp threads of the cloth. Each panel shall be .$t&&cl and fastened in a au&able specimen-holding frame. i ~N0T.E - Such a frame is made by using a 1 m length of corrosion-resistant wire ( for example, tinned MS. ) approximately I.7 mm in diameter, bent to form a rectangle. having inside dimensions of 15x30 cm. The ends of the wire may overlap about 5 cm at one corner and be fastened together.

A set of three panels is required for each ageing temperature. A suitable fixture shall be used for holding the specimen frames in the oven in a vertical position with a minimum spacing of 2'5 cm. 3.2 Varnish Dipping and Drying/CuringTest specimens shall be prepared by dipping the mounted glass cloth panels in the varnish at the ambient temperature. The consistency of the varnish shall be adjusted by trial so that two or more coats will give an increase in thickness of 0'08 f 0'005 mm over the cloth thickness. The panel shall be immersed in the varnish in the direction of the 30 cm length until bubbling stops. Tt shall be mechanically withdrawn at a uniform rate of 10 cm/min and allowed to drain for half an hour. _. 4. TEST APPARATUS
4.1 Weighing balance with an accuracy

of 0'001 g.

4.2 Ageing Ovens - The air circulating ovens shall be such that the temperature inside the oven does not vary by more than rt2"C from the specified temperature. 5. AGEING TEMPERATURE
5.1 The specimens AND TIMES

shall be aged at not less than three, and preferably more, ageing temperatures covering sufficient temperature range to establish the relative thermal endurance. The ageing temperature sha'l differ by at least 20C. The lowest ageing temperature shall give a tested thermal life af at least 5 OQO honrs. An ageing temperature giving a thermal We of less than tOQ,hours shouldnotbeusect To reduce the error in extrapolating thermal endurance data and to obtain the temperature index, the lowest ageing t*peratnre. shonld be chosen so that an extrapolation exceeding 20�C should not be necessary. Choose the exposure temperature so that any essentially linear portion of the life data curve ( log of time ta failure v/s the reciprocal of the absolute temperature J is w&l esfabhshed. For suitable exposure temperature ranges and cycle durations, refer Table 1 of rs : 8504 (Part I j-19??? 6. TEST PROCEDURE
63 Test specimens are prepared,

varnished and dried/baked as described in 3 From these specimen samples measuring 10 X IO cm are cut so that three samples per exposure temperature are available for the tests.
6.1 Initially

the individual sample panels are weighed to an accuracy of 0'001 gas the first weight EI, E2and E3and the mean value E is calculated from them. From the weight per unit area of the glass fabric (3.1) (from 93 g/m2 to 140 g/m" depending upon the thickness of glass cloth ), the approximate weight G of the glass filament support for the 10~ 10cm sample is calculated. Finally the value S of the weight of an aged. sample is calculated from the following equation: s = (1 - P)E + P.G where P is the decimal fraction of total permissible, loss in weight, that is, 0'3.
as a guide for the canclusian of ageing t&e NOTE - The value S is required in order to understand the Cnal remaining weight af the test specimen after a fixed loss in weight of the specimen. *Guide for determination of thermal kndurance materials: Part 1 Temperature indices and thermal 5 properties endurance of electricai profiles. insdatkg

IS : 11256 ( Part 2 ) - 1985 6.2 Ageing and Specimen TestingSpecimen shall be suitably tagged or otherwise permanently identified or placed in a suitable holding frames ( see Fig. I ) and placed in the ageing oven and positioned so that it is at least IO cm from the walls at any point and the specimens are held parallel to the direction of the air flow. Specimens shall be removed at the end of the each cycle at respective ageing temperature. After removal, the specimens shall be conditioned for at least 4 hours at 27 & 2�C at standard atmospheric conditions (see IS: 2260-1973*) and then weighed to an accuracy of 0'001 g. The ageing of each sample is continued until its second weight A has fallen below the value S. At the end of ageing, the exact weight G of the glass fabric of each individual sample is determined by burning the specimen over a Bunsen burner or by incineration and weighing the specimen after cooling and conditioning at 17 k 2'C for 4 hours at standard atmospheric conditions. For varnishes which contain pigments, fillers or resins, it is necessary to determine the weight of the unvarnished specimen. 7. LOSS OF MASS END POINT
